chapter: The Dew Drop, Blue Eagle and visiting stars
title: Reviving the Dew Drop; Chris Kenner's key and fallen stars
summary: Attendance rose when he arrived; wrong-key story with Chris Kenner, and stars who later came back down.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: How do you mean it had gone down?

Well, you know, attendance was why people had started going to other places. Because, you know, bad bands always run people. And so after I started playing there, the place came back up. And I stayed there so long. But I said that's why I got to know Frank Fairley well, you know, know where he was coming from. Oh, Chris Kenner. I had an incident with Chris Kenner there. And when Chris Kenner had Sick and Tired, and I had rehearsed Sick and Tired for me, Chris Kenner did it in B-flat and I was doing it in Key of C. And so Frank Pena called Chris up. So I called Chris up to do a tune. And so naturally he wanted to sing his hit record. And I asked him what key. He said he didn't know. And I didn't think. So I played where we played. And it was too high for Chris. And so boy, Chris Kenner was a big Chris Kenner about that wide. Chris Kenner wanted to punch me in the mouth.

You don't get me on all that bad. You don't get me on all that bad. You don't get me on all that bad. Embarrass me. Oh, she cursed words and I didn't say nothing to him. You know, cause the only thing I said, well, he didn't know what key he was singing in. I played it. We played in different keys.
But we finally found his key. But we finally found his key. See? And by the way, dear I must say, it must have been hard. Yeah, yeah.

But here's what happened after that. After Christian went up to the top, come back down, I was the first man he asked for fifty cents to get him a plate of red beans and a dew drop. I didn't give him fifty cents, I gave him a dollar. I gave him a dollar and something to him, get him some red beans and get him a beer. Same way with Cato, you know. Cato, Ernie Cato was this fella, this is an almighty high dude. And when he went down, he went up and you know he came down too. But see, they all passed me, went up, left me where I was. When they came back down, I was still where I was. They had to always come to me for help. And you know, I was always nice to do that. And that's why I said with my good lady friend, you know, she's up there now. And I hope she has sense enough to be able to stay and treat people right because anything that goes up is going to come down. And she will come back down. And I hope she takes care of, you know, a lot of people and have all her business in order when she comes back down because she do have the wrong man in front of her, I think. I think he's wrong. And she's wrong. Although she said nothing really didn't happen until she got with him. But I think it was destined for it to happen for her. And it just so happened she met him. But I don't like him. I don't necessarily like him. He's different. He ain't my cup of tea. Yeah. Yeah.
